note: Content for the library dashboard (Course A: Upcycle Your Old Device). Quotes are verbatim excerpts from public-domain literary works (author dead 70+ years, published pre-1929) — chosen as literal text rather than 'quotes about reading,' since misattributed quotations are common and an excerpt from the actual work carries no attribution risk. Facts are sourced to cpl.org and cross-checked against the Encyclopedia of Cleveland History. Nothing here is invented.

quotes.text: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife.

facts.text: Cleveland Public Library opened on February 17, 1869, with about 5,800 books.
Cleveland Public Library was one of the first large public libraries to let patrons select their own books directly from the shelves, earning it the nickname "The People's University."
Main Library's current building, designed by the Cleveland firm Walker & Weeks, opened in 1925.
The John G. White Collection at Cleveland Public Library grew from a donation of 122 maps in 1884 to more than 161,000 maps and atlases today.
Cleveland Public Library serves the city through Main Library and twenty-seven branch locations.
